<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/deception/installing-landmine-agent-linux","lastmod":"2026-08-03T00:19Z","nid":"1540400"} -->
## Installing a Landmine Agent on Linux

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/installing-landmine-agent-linux
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents > Installing a Landmine Agent on Linux
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to install a landmine agent on the Linux platform using the command line interface (CLI).

This article provides instructions for installing a landmine agent on the Linux platform using the command line interface (CLI).

You can run a landmine agent on the desktop versions of Linux operating systems. Headless server operating systems are not supported.

## Prerequisites

Before installing a landmine agent, make sure you have:

- Endpoints running 64-bit (AMD64 or x86_64) versions of supported Linux distributions:
  - Debian 10 or later
  - Ubuntu 20.04 or later LTS releases
  - Red Hat Enterprise Linux version 8 or later
  - Fedora 35 or later
  - openSUSE Leap 15.3 or later
- Network connectivity from the endpoints where the agent is installed to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal instance on port 443. This connection is proxy aware, and you can optionally define a list of proxies for the agent to connect through.

## Installing a Landmine Agent on Linux Using the RPM Package

To install a landmine agent on Linux (rpm):

1. [Download the Linux (rpm) installer](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/downloading-landmine-agents) file from the Deception Admin Portal.
2. Create a text file (`landmine.txt`) in the `tmp` folder. To create a file:
  1. Open a terminal window.
  2. Use a text editor (e.g., Vi or Nano) to create a text file.
3. Copy the Deception Admin Portal's instance name and the Agent Registration Token from the **Download Landmine Agent** window and paste it into the text file: See image.
4. Run the following command in a terminal from the path where the .rpm file is downloaded: sudo rpm -ivh/tmp/Landmine.rpm

## Installing a Landmine Agent on Linux Using the DEB Package

To install a landmine agent on Linux (deb):

1. [Download the Linux (deb) installer](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/downloading-landmine-agents) file from the Deception Admin Portal.
2. Create a text file (`landmine.txt`) in the `tmp` folder. To create a file:
  1. Open a terminal window.
  2. Use a text editor (e.g., Vi or Nano) to create a text file.
3. Copy the Deception Admin Portal's instance name and the Agent Registration Token from the **Download Landmine Agent** window and paste it into the text file: See image.
4. Run the following command in a terminal from the path where the .rpm file is downloaded: sudo dpkg -i/tmp/Landmine.deb

### Configuring Proxies

To configure proxies for Linux, add the proxy definition to the text file (`/tmp/landmine.txt`). To configure multiple proxies, add a list of proxies separated by commas.

For example:

```
<instance name>
<Agent Registration Token>
http://user:password@proxy-server:8888,http://proxy-server:3128
```

When the landmine agent starts, it attempts to connect to the Deception Admin Portal using the list of proxies in a sequence from left to right. If the proxy is not configured, the agent attempts to connect to the portal directly.

After you run the command, the landmine agent connects to the portal using one of the following methods:

- Connects via `http://user:password@proxy-server:8888/proxy`.
- Connects via `http://proxy-server:3128/proxy`.

If all of the above methods fail, the agent attempts to connect to the portal using a direct no-proxy connection.

You can configure proxies using the following URL format:

```
http://[username:password]@
<ip/host>
:
<port>
```

If the username and password have special characters (e.g., Username = user#2211 and password = pass@123), you must URL-encode them. For example:

```
http://user%232211:pass%40123@proxy-server-1:8888
```

Example proxy URLs:

- `http://192.0.2.2:3128/`: Connect to a proxy server with an IP address = 192.0.2.2 and port number = 3128.
- `http://proxy-server:8888/`: Connect to a proxy server with the DNS name = proxy-server and port number = 8888.
- `http://proxyuser:proxypassword@192.0.2.18:3128/`: Connect to a proxy server with an IP address = 192.0.2.18, port number = 3128, username = proxyuser, and password = proxypassword.
- `http://user%232211:pass%40123@proxy-server-1:8888/`: Connect to a proxy server with the DNS name = proxy-server, port number = 8888, username= user#2211, and password = pass@123.

[Image: Download landmine agent Linux (rpm) installer]

[Image: Download landmine agent Linux (deb) installer]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/deception/installing-landmine-agent-macos","lastmod":"2026-08-03T00:19Z","nid":"1540387"} -->
## Installing a Landmine Agent on macOS

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/installing-landmine-agent-macos
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents > Installing a Landmine Agent on macOS
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to install a landmine agent on macOS.

This article provides instructions for installing a landmine agent on the macOS platform using the CLI.

Beginning with version 4.32, the following changes apply:

- You can install Landmine Agents using the .pkg file even if the endpoints have existing Landmine Agents. The new version of Landmine Agent overwrites the previous installation and moves it to the `/opt/` directory regardless of the previous location. The service name is retained from the previous installation regardless of the current configuration.
- The `uninstall.sh` script is no longer part of the Landmine Agent installation packages. The existing `uninstall.sh` script file is removed when the Landmine Agent is updated. Uninstallation of Landmine Agents via the Deception Admin Portal and manual removal using the command (`sudo <PATH_TO_updater> landmine remove`) continue to be supported.

## Prerequisites

Before installing a landmine agent, ensure that you have:

- A Mac computer with macOS Ventura (version 13) or later.
- Network connectivity from the system where the agent is installed to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal instance on port 443. This connection is proxy-aware, and you can optionally define a list of proxies for the agent to connect through.
- (Optional) Enabled Full Disk Access for the agent. This is required to use the Defense Evasion, file decoy events, brute force login detections, and process tree functionality in other features.
  - Steps to grant Full Disk Access for manual installs.
  - Snippet to grant Full Disk Access that can be added to the MDM profile.

## Installing Landmine Agent on macOS

To install a Landmine Agent on macOS:

1. [Download the macOS installer (Intel or Apple Silicon)](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/downloading-landmine-agents) file from the Deception Admin Portal.
2. Create a text file (`landmine.txt`) in the `/tmp` folder.
3. Copy the Deception Admin Portal's instance name and the agent registration token from the **Download Landmine Agent** window and paste it into the text file. See image.
4. Run the following command in a terminal from the path where the .pkg file is downloaded: For Intel-based macOS endpoints: sudo installer -pkg Landmine_Intel.pkg -target /For Apple Silicon-based macOS endpoints: sudo installer -pkg Landmine_AppleSilicon.pkg -target /

## Configuring Proxies

To configure proxies for macOS, add the proxy definition to the text file (`/tmp/landmine.txt`). To configure multiple proxies, add a list of proxies separated by commas.

For example:

```
<instance name>
<Agent Registration Token>
http://user:password@proxy-server:8888,http://proxy-server:3128
```

When the landmine agent starts, it attempts to connect to the Deception Admin Portal using the list of proxies in a sequence from left to right. Finally, the agent tries to connect directly without a proxy.

After you run the command, the landmine agent connects to the portal using one of the following methods:

- Connects via `http://user:password@proxy-server:8888/proxy`.
- Connects via `http://proxy-server:3128/proxy`.

If all of the above methods fail, the agent attempts to connect to the portal using a direct no-proxy connection.

You can configure proxies using the following URL format:

```
http://[username:password]@
<ip/host>
:
<port>
```

If the username and password have special characters (e.g., Username = user#2211 and password = pass@123), you must URL-encode them. For example:

```
http://user%232211:pass%40123@proxy-server-1:8888
```

Example proxy URLs:

- `http://192.0.2.2:3128/`: Connect to a proxy server with an IP address = 192.0.2.2 and port number = 3128.
- `http://proxy-server:8888/`: Connect to a proxy server with the DNS name = proxy-server and port number = 8888.
- `http://proxyuser:proxypassword@192.0.2.18:3128/`: Connect to a proxy server with an IP address = 192.0.2.18, port number = 3128, username = proxyuser, and password = proxypassword.
- `http://user%232211:pass%40123@proxy-server-1:8888/`: Connect to a proxy server with the DNS name = proxy-server, port number = 8888, username= user#2211, and password = pass@123.

[Image: A screenshot capturing the Download Landmine Agent window with macOS-specific tabs highlighted]

1. In the macOS endpoint, go to **System Settings**> **Privacy & Security**> **Full Disk Access**.
2. Enable the toggle for `XPCServerApp.app`.
3. Reboot the machine.

A profile with a Full Disk Access grant must be deployed before installing Landmine Agents. After installing the Landmine Agent, the machine must be rebooted.

```
<key>SystemPolicyAllFiles</key> 
	<array> 
		<dict> 
			<key>Allowed</key> 
			<true/> 
			<key>CodeRequirement</key> 
			<string>identifier "com.zscaler.deception.XPCServerApp" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = PCBCQZJ7S7</string> 
			<key>Identifier</key> 
			<string>com.zscaler.deception.XPCServerApp</string> 
			<key>IdentifierType</key> 
			<string>bundleID</string> 
			<key>StaticCode</key> 
			<false/> 
		</dict> 
	</array>
```
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/deception/installing-landmine-agent-using-active-directory-gpo","lastmod":"2026-08-03T00:19Z","nid":"1540544"} -->
## Installing a Landmine Agent Using an Active Directory Group Policy Object

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/installing-landmine-agent-using-active-directory-gpo
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents > Installing a Landmine Agent Using an Active Directory Group Policy Object
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to install a landmine agent on domain-joined user machines using Active Directory’s (AD) Group Policy Object (GPO).

You can install a landmine agent on domain-joined user machines using Active Directory (AD) Group Policy Object (GPO).

## Prerequisites

Before installing a landmine agent, make sure that the following prerequisites are met:

- Windows installer and .NET framework For Windows 10 version 1607 and earlier, install the latest version of the .NET framework for the installation to succeed. Microsoft Windows 7, Windows 8, and Windows 8.1 are not supported.
  - 64-bit versions of Windows 10 or later
  - .NET version 4.6.1 or later (Zscaler recommends using the latest version of .NET framework)
- RAM: 100 MB of free memory
- Storage: 1 GB of free storage, preferably in an SSD
- Network Connectivity: A minimum of 256 Kbps internet bandwidth and an open outbound port 443 on the system where the agent is installed to connect to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. This connection is proxy-aware, and you can either use a statically defined proxy or the proxy configured for the `SYSTEM` user.

The resource requirements listed here are also the landmine agent's maximum limits of utilization.

## Installing a Landmine Agent Using an Active Directory

To install a landmine agent using an AD GPO:

1. [Download the Windows EXE installer](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/downloading-landmine-agents) file and copy the installation command from the Deception Admin Portal. See image.
2. Create a batch file using the following installation command: Landmine.exe /qn CMC=<Deception Admin Portal instance> REGKEY=<Key> /l*v <Path to Landmine installation logs>The command must contain the complete path of the landmine EXE installer if it is stored in a shared folder. The last part of the command `/l*v <Path to Landmine installation logs>` is optional.; If a proxy is required to access the Zscaler Deception from endpoints, then add the proxy parameters to the installation command. To learn more, see [Installing a Landmine Agent on Windows](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/installing-landmine-agent-windows).
3. Press the `Windows key+R` in your domain controller (DC).
4. In the **Run** window, enter `gpmc.msc` to open the Group Policy Management console.
5. Create or select a GPO on which you want to install the landmine agent. To create a GPO, refer to the [Microsoft Technical documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/network-security/windows-firewall/create-a-group-policy-object).
6. Go to **Computer configuration** > **Policies** > **Windows settings** > **Scripts (Startup/Shutdown)**.
7. In the **Scripts (Startup/Shutdown)**pane, double-click **Startup**. See image.
8. In the **Startup Properties** window, click **Show Files** to open the **Startup** folder. See image.
9. Copy the landmine EXE installer and batch files. See image.
10. In the **Startup Properties** window, click **Add** and select the landmine batch file. See image.
11. Click **OK**.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/deception/installing-landmine-agent-windows","lastmod":"2026-08-03T00:19Z","nid":"1540384"} -->
## Installing a Landmine Agent on Windows

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/installing-landmine-agent-windows
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents > Installing a Landmine Agent on Windows
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to install a landmine agent on the Windows platform using the command line interface (CLI).

This article provides instructions for installing a landmine agent on the Windows platform using the command line interface (CLI).

## Prerequisites

Before installing a landmine agent, ensure that your endpoints have:

- Windows 10 (64-bit only) or Windows 11 (64-bit only) with Windows Installer and .NET version 4.6.1 or later Microsoft Windows 7, Windows 8, and Windows 8.1 are not supported.; Zscaler recommends using the latest version of .NET framework. For Windows 10 version 1607 and earlier, installing the latest version of the .NET framework is mandatory for the installation to succeed.
- 100 MB of free memory
- 1 GB of free storage, preferably in an SSD
- A minimum of 256 Kbps internet bandwidth and an open outbound port 443 on the system where the agent is installed to connect to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. This connection is proxy ware, and you can either use a statically defined proxy or the proxy configured for the `SYSTEM` user.

The resource requirements listed here are also the landmine agent's maximum limits of utilization.

## Installing a Landmine Agent on Windows

You can install a landmine agent on a single or multiple systems. If you install an agent on multiple systems, use a deployment management tool, such as Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM) (formerly known as Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM)). Zscaler recommends installing landmine agents on a few systems prior to a broader deployment.

You can run the installation commands on an administrator command prompt, or use an automation tool that runs the commands as an administrator.

To install a landmine agent on Windows:

1. [Download the Windows EXE installer](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/downloading-landmine-agents) file from the Deception Admin Portal.
2. Start a command prompt as an administrator.
  1. Click **Start**.
  2. In the **Start Search** box, enter `cmd`, and then press `CTRL+SHIFT+ENTER`.
  3. When the **User Account Control** (UAC) dialog box appears, click **Yes**.
3. In the command prompt, choose a command per your installation requirements:
  - Enter the following command to install the agent without proxies or debug logs: Landmine.exe /qn CMC=<instance name> REGKEY=<Registration Token>
  - Enter the following command to install the landmine agent with debug logs stored in the `C:\agent-install.log` file: Landmine.exe /qn CMC=<instance name> REGKEY=<Registration Token> /l*v C:\agent-install.log
  - Enter the following command to install the landmine agent with a proxy: Landmine.exe /qn CMC=<instance name> REGKEY=<Registration Token> PROXIES=http://proxy-server:3128The standalone landmine agent is a proxy-aware application. It can automatically detect and apply the proxy configurations if they are already available in the system.

The following table describes the installation parameters:

| Parameter | Description | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/qn` | Enables silent mode installation | Yes |
| `CMC=<instance name>` | The hostname of the Deception Admin Portal | Yes |
| `REGKEY=<Registration Token>` | The Agent Registration Token | Yes |
| `PROXIES=<Proxy String>` | Proxies to connect to the Deception Admin Portal. If there is more than one proxy, separate them with a comma. Make sure that there are no white spaces in the `PROXIES` parameter. | No |
| `/l*v <Path to Log File>` | Enables verbose logging and sets the destination log file path | No |

After you run the command, the landmine agent is installed and appears in the **Agents** table (**Settings**> **Endpoint Settings**> **Agents**).

### Configuring Proxies

The standalone landmine agent is a proxy-aware application. It can automatically detect and apply the proxy configurations if they are already available in the system.

You can use the `PROXIES` parameter in the installation command to configure multiple proxies. The `PROXIES` parameter consists of a list of proxies separated by commas. When the landmine agent starts, it attempts to connect to the Deception Admin Portal using the list of proxies in a sequence from left to right. If the proxy is not configured, the agent attempts to connect to the Deception Admin Portal directly, or it uses a proxy configured for the `SYSTEM` user.

To configure multiple proxies, open the command prompt and enter the following command:

```
Landmine.exe /qn CMC=
<instance name>
REGKEY=
<Registration Token>
PROXIES=http://proxy-server/proxy.pac,http://user:password@proxy-server:8888,http://proxy-server:3128
```

After you run the command, the landmine agent connects to the Deception Admin Portal using one of the following methods:

- Downloads the PAC file from `http://proxy-server/proxy.pac` and uses the PAC file configuration to establish the connection.
- Connects via `http://user:password@proxy-server:8888/proxy`.
- Connects via `http://proxy-server:3128/proxy`.

If all of the above methods fail, the agent attempts to connect to the Deception Admin Portal using the `SYSTEM` users proxy. If this also fails, the agent attempts a direct no-proxy connection.

You can configure proxies using the following URL format:

```
http://
[username:password]
@
<ip/host>
:
<port>
```

If the username and password have special characters (e.g., Username = user#2211 and password = pass@123), you must URL-encode them. For example:

```
http://user%232211:pass%40123@proxy-server-1:8888
```

You can perform URL encoding using the following PowerShell function:

```
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Web; [System.Web.HttpUtility]::UrlEncode(
<string>
)
```

[Image: URL encoding using the PowerShell function]

Example proxy URLs:

- `http://192.0.2.2:3128/`: Connect to a proxy server with an IP address = 192.0.2.2 and port number = 3128.
- `http://proxy-server:8888/`: Connect to a proxy server with the DNS name = proxy-server and port number = 8888.
- `http://proxyuser:proxypassword@192.0.2.18:3128/`: Connect to a proxy server with an IP address = 192.0.2.18, port number = 3128, username = proxyuser, and password = proxypassword.
- `http://user%232211:pass%40123@proxy-server-1:8888/`: Connect to a proxy server with the DNS name = proxy-server, port number = 8888, username= user#2211, and password = pass@123.

### Configuring Proxies to Use a PAC File

To configure a proxy to use a PAC file, you must direct the landmine agent to a URL where the PAC file is hosted.

You can configure a proxy using the following URL format:

```
http://
<ip/host>
/
<pacfile>
.pac
```

Example PAC file URLs:

- `http://192.0.2.6/proxy.pac`: Connect to an HTTP server with an IP address = 192.0.2.6 and download the proxy.pac file.
- `http://pac-server/proxies.pac`: Connect to an HTTP server with the DNS name = pac-server and download the proxies.pac file.
- `http://pac-server:33234/proxy.pac`: Connect to an HTTP server with the DNS name = pac-server, port number = 33234, and download the proxy file.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/deception/installing-landmine-agents-windows-using-mecm-or-sccm","lastmod":"2026-08-03T00:19Z","nid":"1540399"} -->
## Installing Landmine Agents on Windows Using MECM or SCCM

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/installing-landmine-agents-windows-using-mecm-or-sccm
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents > Installing Landmine Agents on Windows Using MECM or SCCM
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to install a landmine agent on the Windows platform using MECM or SCCM.

This article provides instructions for installing a landmine agent on the Windows platform using Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM) (formerly known as Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM)).

## Prerequisites

Before installing a landmine agent, make sure that the following prerequisites are met:

- Windows installer and .NET framework Microsoft Windows 7, Windows 8, and Windows 8.1 are not supported.
  - 64-bit versions of Windows 10
  - .NET version 4.6.1 or later (Zscaler recommends using the latest version of .NET framework)
  - All Windows 10 editions include the .NET framework as an OS component.
- You must have a network file share that is accessible to all systems. This can be the system volume (SYSVOL) file share or any other file share that is accessible to all systems where the landmine agents are deployed.
- RAM: 100 MB of free memory
- Storage: 1 GB of free storage, preferably in an SSD
- Network Connectivity: A minimum of 256 Kbps internet bandwidth and an open port 443 on the systems where the agent is installed to connect to the Zscaler Deception. This connection is proxy-aware, and you can either use a statically defined proxy or the proxy configured for the `SYSTEM` user.

The resource requirements listed here are also the landmine agent's maximum limits of utilization.

## Installing Agents on Windows Using MECM

Do not use the Windows MSI Installer with MECM. The landmine agents may not install properly using the MECM built-in MSI installation method.

To install a landmine agent on the Windows platform using MECM:

- Step 1: Download and Publish the Installer
- Step 2: Create an Application
- Step 3: Deploy the Application

1. [Download the Windows EXE installer file](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/downloading-landmine-agents) from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.
2. Copy the EXE file to a file share that is accessible to all systems or users.

1. Open MECM.
2. Go to **Software Library** > **Overview** > **Application Management** > **Applications**.
3. In the **Applications pane**, right-click on a blank area and select **Create Application**.
4. After the **Create Application Wizard** opens, on the **General** page, select **Manually specify the application information.**
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **General Information** page:
  1. **Name**: Enter the name of the application.
  2. **Software version**: Enter the software version of the EXE file and click **Next**.
7. On the **Deployment Types** page, click **Add** to create a new deployment type.
8. After the **Create Deployment Types Wizard** opens, on the **General** page:
  1. **Type**: Select **Script Installer** from the drop-down menu.
  2. Select **Manually specify the deployment type information**.
  3. Click **Next**.
9. On the **General Information** page, enter a **Name** for the deployment type.
10. On the **Content** page:
  1. **Content location**: Browse the location that contains the `Landmine.exe` file.
  2. **Installation program**: Enter "`Landmine.exe" /qn CMC=``<Deception Admin Portal instance name>``REGKEY=``<Registration Token>`.
  3. **Uninstallation program**: Enter `msiexec /qn /x {94e4ac3b-2519-46eb-97bd-d6be9b6c8f55}`.
  4. Click **Next**.
11. On the **Detection Method** page, click **Add Clause** to add a detection clause.
12. On the **Detection Rule** page:
  1. **Setting Type**: Select **File System** from the drop-down menu.
  2. **Type**: Select **File** from the drop-down menu.
  3. **Path**: Enter or browse to the path where the landmine agent must be installed. This is usually `C:\ProgramData\``<Service name>`, where <`Service name>` is the name of the service specified in the Deception Admin Portal.
  4. **File or folder name**: Enter `<Service name>``.exe`.
  5. Unselect **This file or folder is associated with a 32-bit application on 64-bit systems**.
  6. Click **OK**.
13. On the **User Experience** page: The application is created. If the landmine service is renamed in the Deception Admin Portal, you must add a new detection clause to the system. Do not remove the existing detection clause as that might cause existing agents to not be detected.
  1. **Installer behavior**: Select **Install for system** from the drop-down menu.
  2. **Installation program visibility**: Select **Hidden**.
  3. Click **Next**.

1. Open MECM.
2. Go to **Software Library** > **Overview** > **Application Management** > **Applications**.
3. Select the application that you created and right-click.
4. Select **Deploy** from the menu.
5. After the **Deploy Software Wizard** opens, on the **General** page, select **All Desktops and Server Clients** from the**Collection** drop-down menu.
6. Click **Next**.
7. On the **Content** page, click **Add** to distribute the content for this application to a distribution point or a distribution point group.
8. On the **Deployment Settings** page, in the **Purpose**field, select **Required** from the drop-down menu.
9. Click **Next**.
10. (Optional) On the **Scheduling** page, set a deployment schedule.
11. On the **User Experience** page, in the **User notifications** field, select **Hide in Software Center and all notifications** from the drop-down menu.
12. Click **Next**.
13. Complete the application deployment.

The application is deployed. The value under **Compliance %** changes after the agents are deployed.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/deception/managing-advanced-settings","lastmod":"2026-08-03T00:19Z","nid":"1540453"} -->
## Managing Advanced Setting

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/managing-advanced-settings
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Settings > Managing Advanced Setting
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to manage Advanced Settings in the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

Advanced Settings allow you to view license details, manage events logs and evidence files, configure a retention policy for logs, and more.

To view and manage advanced settings:

1. Go to **Settings** > **Advanced Settings**.
2. Select any of the following options:
  - License
  - Manage Events & Evidence
  - Retention
  - Show/Hide Internal Components

On the License tab, you can view the details of your current Deception license:

- **Client**: The customer name the license is issued to.
- **Plan**: The active Deception subscription plan your organization is licensed to.
- **Expiration**: The expiration date of your current subscribed license.
- **Retention Policy**: The number of days after which all events and evidence files are permanently deleted.
- **Decoys**: The number of decoys configured out of the total decoys included in your subscription plan.
- **Landmine Users**: The number of users that have landmine configured out of the total landmine users included in your subscription plan.
- **Admin Portal Version**: The current version of Deception.

See image.

On the Manage Events & Evidence tab, do the following.

- Export Event Logs
- Delete Event Logs
- Download an Evidence File
- Delete an Evidence File

On the Retention tab, you can configure the retention period to store event logs, audit logs, etc. The retention policy is defined in the Deception license agreement. The default retention period is 365 days, and it can be reduced if required. Data is permanently deleted after the retention period expires.

The retention period of the following events or logs cannot be modified:

- Events that are [marked as safe](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/taking-action-from-the-dashboard) are retained for 7 days.
- Okta system logs for threat detection are retained for 14 days.

To configure the retention period:

1. On the **Retention**tab, enter the retention period in days. See image.
2. Click **Save**.

To export event logs:

1. On the **Manage Events & Evidence**tab, under **Export Events (Serializable JSON)**, select a date and time from the **From** and **To** drop-down menus. See image.
2. Click **Export**. The event logs are downloaded to your system in the JSON format.

To delete event logs that are marked as safe, or delete all event logs for a specified time frame.:

1. On the **Manage Events & Evidence**, under **Delete Events**, select a date and time from the **From** and **To** drop-down menus.
2. Select an option: See image.
  - **All Events**: All the events for the specified time frame are deleted.
  - **Marked as safe only**: Only events that are marked as safe are deleted.
3. Click **Delete**. The event logs for the specified time frame are deleted.

To download an evidence file from a Decoy Connector:

1. On the **Manage Events & Evidence**tab, under **Download & Delete Evidence**, select a date and time from the **From** and **To** drop-down menus.
2. Select a Decoy Connector from the drop-down menu.
3. Select the evidence type (e.g., select **pcap**). See image.
4. Click **Download**. The evidence file is downloaded to your local system.

To delete an evidence file from a Decoy Connector:

1. On the **Manage Events & Evidence**tab, under **Download & Delete Evidence**, select a date and time from the **From** and **To** drop-down menus.
2. Select a Decoy Connector from the drop-down menu.
3. Select the evidence type (e.g., select **ioc**). See image.
4. Click **Delete**.
5. Click **OK** in the confirmation window. The evidence file for the specified time frame is deleted.

The download and delete evidence operations trigger a download of up to 10,000 files or 3 GB of uncompressed evidence at a time. You might have to run these operations multiple times to clear evidence for large date ranges.

The Zscaler Deception Admin Portal uses the Private Access (ZPA) service to deploy decoys in a dedicated Zscaler Deception cloud. To learn more, see [Understanding the Zscaler Deception Architecture](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/understanding-zscaler-deception-architecture). You can show or hide Private Access components, such as Private Access Decoy Connectors and interfaces, in the Deception Admin Portal.

To show Private Access interfaces:

1. On the **Show/Hide Internal Components**tab, enable **Show internal components**. See image.
2. Click **Save**.
3. Go to **Settings** > **Topology** > **Interfaces**. The Private Access interfaces appear on the **Interfaces** page. See image.

[Image: Show or hide internal components]

[Image: View ZPA components]

[Image: Download evidence file]

[Image: Delete an evidence file]

[Image: View Deception license details]

[Image: Export events logs]

[Image: Delete event logs]

[Image: Configure retention period]

[Image: View Advanced Settings tabs]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Managing Agent Update Groups

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/managing-agent-update-groups
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agent Update Groups > Managing Agent Update Groups
- Last modified: 2024-05-18T07:06Z
- Summary: How to manage landmine agent groups, including enabling or disabling phased updates, downloading the agent groups update status as a CSV file, exporting hostnames, and editing or deleting an agent group.

You can manage agent update groups using the various options under the **Actions**column in the agents table.

## Enabling or Disabling Updates

To enable or disable the updates for a specific agent update group:

1. Go to **Settings**> **Endpoint Settings**> **Agent Update Groups**.
2. Locate the agent update group for which you want to enable or disable updates, and click the **X** icon or the checkmark icon under the **Actions**column to disable or enable phased updates respectively for an agent update group. See image. You can see the status of each group and how many endpoints have been updated in the table.

## Downloading Status Details of Agent Update Groups

You can download the update status details of an agent update group as a CSV file.

To download update status details of an agent update group:

1. Go to **Settings**> **Endpoint Settings**> **Agent Update Groups**.
2. Locate the agent update group for which you want to download the update details, and click the **Download**icon under the **Actions**column. See image. A CSV file with the agent group update status is downloaded to your system. See image.

## Editing an Agent Update Group

To edit an agent update group:

1. Go to **Settings**> **Endpoint Settings**> **Agent Update Groups**.
2. Locate the agent update group that you want to edit, and click the **Edit**icon under the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Agent Update Group** **Details**window, make the necessary changes. See image.
4. Click **Save**.

## Exporting Hostnames

You can export the list of hostnames associated with an agent update group as a TXT file.

To export hostnames from an agent update group:

1. Go to **Settings**> **Endpoint Settings**> **Agent Update Groups**.
2. Locate the agent update group that you want to export, and click the **Edit**icon under the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Agent Update Group Details** window, click **Export hostnames**. See image. A TXT file containing the list of hostnames is downloaded to your system.

## Deleting an Agent Update Group

To delete an agent update group:

1. Go to **Settings**> **Endpoint Settings**> **Agent Update Groups**.
2. Locate the agent update group that you want to delete, and click the **Delete**icon under the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the confirmation window, click **OK**. The agent update group is deleted.

## Managing AWS Decoys

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/managing-aws-decoys
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Deceive  > Cloud Deception > AWS > Managing AWS Decoys
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to manage AWS decoys, including checking status and editing or deleting them.

You can manage your Amazon Web Services (AWS) decoys from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. All decoys created from the Deception Admin Portal are tabulated under their respective decoy category tabs. Each table shows the details associated with each decoy in the category and its deployment status. You can also edit or delete decoys by using the respective options from the decoys table.

## Checking Deployment Status

At the time of integration, Zscaler Deception deploys a health check lambda function on AWS. This function periodically checks all decoy resources deployed on AWS and updates their status to the Deception Admin Portal every 15 minutes. You can check the deployment status indicated by the icon next to the name of the decoy in the decoys table. The following icons are used to show the status of the decoys:

- [Image: Green status icon]– Indicates a deployed state.
- [Image: Orange status icon]– Indicates an inactive state. This means the decoy no longer exists on AWS or one of its properties used to reference does not exist. This happens when the decoy or its resources are manipulated directly from AWS.
- [Image: Grey status icon]– Indicates a pending deployment state. This means that the decoy has been created or modified in the Deception Admin Portal, but the deployment script to propagate changes to the AWS cloud has not been initiated.
- [Image: Red status icon]– Indicates a pending deletion state. This means that the decoy has been deleted from the Deception Admin Portal, but the deployment script to propagate changes to the AWS cloud has not been initiated.

See image.

## Editing or Deleting AWS Decoys

You can edit or delete the AWS decoys that you configured in the Deception Admin Portal. Such changes made to the AWS decoys in the Deception Admin Portal are propagated to the AWS cloud only after running the deployment script on AWS CloudShell.

### Prerequisites

Ensure that you have obtained the CloudShell command using one of the following methods:

- [Automated Download Method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-aws#zd-direct-download-script-aws)
- [Manual Download Method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-aws#zd-manual-download-script-aws)

This only applies to the CloudShell-based deployment.

### Editing an AWS Decoy

To edit an AWS decoy:

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **AWS**.
2. Select the relevant decoy category tab. For example, if you want to edit an IAM user decoy, select the **IAM**tab. See image.
3. Make sure that the decoy you want to edit isn't deployed, and then click the **Edit**icon for the decoy.
4. Modify the decoy details as per your requirements.
5. Click **Save**.
6. Deploy the changes based on the method used to configure the integration between AWS and Deception: Upon successful execution, the changes are propagated to the AWS cloud.
  - Terraform-based deployment
  - CloudShell-based deployment

### Deleting an AWS Decoy

To delete an AWS decoy:

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **AWS**.
2. Select the relevant decoy category tab. For example, if you want to delete an IAM user decoy, select the **IAM**tab. See image.
3. Locate the decoy you want to delete, and click the **Delete**icon.
4. Deploy the changes based on the method used to configure the integration between AWS and Deception: Upon successful execution, the changes are propagated to the AWS cloud.
  - Terraform-based deployment
  - CloudShell-based deployment

1. On the **Cloud Deception - AWS** page, go to **Settings**.
2. Locate the AWS account you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
4. Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the `aws-decoys.tf.json` file in a text editor.
5. Locate the `backend` block in the `aws-decoys.tf.json` file. Add your back-end details and save the file. The following example shows a `backend` block of an S3 bucket-based Terraform back end: `{ "terraform": { "backend": { "s3": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate", "region": "us-east-1", "encrypt": true } } } }`Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same AWS account.
6. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
7. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
8. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted.
9. The necessary resources are deployed, and a JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
10. On the **Cloud Deception - AWS** page, go to **Settings**, locate the AWS account you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.

## Managing Azure Decoys

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/managing-azure-decoys
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Deceive  > Cloud Deception > Azure > Managing Azure Decoys
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: Information on how to manage Azure decoys.

You can manage your Microsoft Azure decoys from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. All decoys created from the Deception Admin Portal are tabulated under their respective decoy category tabs. Each table shows the details associated with each decoy in the category and also shows its deployment status. You can also edit or delete decoys by using the respective options from the decoys table.

## Checking Deployment Status

At the time of integration, Zscaler Deception deploys a health check function on Azure. This function periodically checks all decoy resources deployed on Azure and updates their status to the Deception Admin Portal every 15 minutes. You can check the deployment status indicated by the icon next to the name of the decoy in the decoys table. The following icons are used to show the status of the decoys:

- [Image: Green status icon]– Indicates a deployed state.
- [Image: Orange status icon]– Indicates an inactive state. This means the decoy no longer exists on Azure or one of its properties used to reference does not exist. This happens when the decoy or its resources are manipulated directly from Azure.
- [Image: Grey status icon]– Indicates a pending deployment state. This means that the decoy has been created or modified in the Deception Admin Portal, but the deployment script to propagate changes to the Azure Cloud has not been initiated.
- [Image: Red status icon]– Indicates a pending deletion state. This means that the decoy has been deleted from the Deception Admin Portal, but the deployment script to propagate changes to the Azure Cloud has not been initiated.

See image.

## Editing or Deleting Azure Decoys

You can edit or delete the Azure decoys that you configured in the Deception Admin Portal. Such changes made to the Azure decoys in the Deception Admin Portall are propagated to the Azure Cloud only after running the deployment script on the Azure Cloud Shell.

### Prerequisites

Obtain the PowerShell command using one of the following methods:

- [Automated Download Method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-direct-download-script)
- [Manual Download Method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-manual-download-script)

This only applies to the Cloud Shell-based deployment.

### Editing an Azure Decoy

To edit an Azure decoy:

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **Azure**.
2. Select the relevant decoy category tab. For example, if you want to edit a user decoy, select the **User**tab.
3. Make sure that the decoy you want to edit is in the **Not Deployed** state, and then click the **Edit**icon. See image.
4. Modify the decoy details as per your requirements.
5. Click **Save**.
6. Deploy the changes based on the method used to configure the integration between Azure and Deception:
  - Terraform-based deployment
  - Cloud Shell-based deployment

Upon successful execution, the changes are propagated to the Azure Cloud.

1. On the **Cloud Deception - Azure**page, go to **Settings**.
2. Locate the Azure account you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
4. Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the `azure-decoys.tf.json` file in a text editor.
5. Locate the `backend` block in the `azure-decoys.tf.json` file. Add your back-end details and save the file. The following example shows a `backend` block of an Azure blob storage-based Terraform back end: `{ "terraform": { "backend": { "azurerm": { "resource_group_name": "your-tfstate-rg", "storage_account_name": "yourtfstatestorageacct", "container_name": "tfstate", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate" } } } }`Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same Azure account.
6. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
7. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
8. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted. The necessary resources are deployed.
9. Run the following command to download the details of the state as a JSON file. `terraform output -json decoys_output > deployment-output.json`A JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
10. On the **Cloud Deception - Azure**page, go to **Settings**, locate the Azure account you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
11. Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.

1. Sign in to the [Azure Portal](http://https//portal.azure.com) as a Cloud Device Administrator or Global Administrator.
2. Launch Cloud Shell by clicking the **Cloud Shell**icon on the top navigation bar. See image. The **Cloud Shell**window appears.
3. In the **Cloud Shell**window: See image.
  1. Set your shell environment to PowerShell.
  2. Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the [automated download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-direct-download-script) or [manual download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-manual-download-script).
  3. Enter the option to deploy the preferred decoy and press `Enter`.

### Deleting an Azure Decoy

To delete an Azure decoy:

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **Azure**.
2. Select the relevant decoy category tab. For example, if you want to delete a user decoy, select the **User**tab.
3. Locate the decoy you want to delete, and click the **Delete**icon. See image.
4. Deploy the changes based on the method used to configure the integration between Azure and Deception:
  - Terraform-based deployment
  - Cloud Shell-based deployment

Upon successful execution, the changes are propagated to the Azure Cloud.

1. On the **Cloud Deception - Azure**page, go to **Settings**.
2. Locate the Azure account you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
4. Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the `azure-decoys.tf.json` file in a text editor.
5. Locate the `backend` block in the `azure-decoys.tf.json` file. Add your back-end details and save the file. The following example shows a `backend` block of an Azure blob storage-based Terraform back end: `{ "terraform": { "backend": { "azurerm": { "resource_group_name": "your-tfstate-rg", "storage_account_name": "yourtfstatestorageacct", "container_name": "tfstate", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate" } } } }`Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same Azure account.
6. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
7. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
8. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted. The necessary resources are deployed.
9. Run the following command to download the details of the state as a JSON file. `terraform output -json decoys_output > deployment-output.json`A JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
10. On the **Cloud Deception - Azure**page, go to **Settings**, locate the Azure account you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
11. Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.

1. Sign in to the [Azure Portal](http://https//portal.azure.com) as a Cloud Device Administrator or Global Administrator.
2. Launch Cloud Shell by clicking the **Cloud Shell**icon on the top navigation bar. See image. The **Cloud Shell**window appears.
3. In the **Cloud Shell**window: See image.
  1. Set your shell environment to PowerShell.
  2. Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the [automated download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-direct-download-script) or [manual download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-manual-download-script).
  3. Enter the option to deploy the preferred decoy and press `Enter`.

## Managing Cloud Deception Settings for an AWS Account

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/managing-cloud-deception-settings-aws-account
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Deceive  > Cloud Deception > AWS > Managing Cloud Deception Settings for an AWS Account
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to edit or delete an AWS Cloud Deception account.

You can edit or delete Cloud Deception settings configured for your Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

## Editing an AWS Account

Depending on whether the configurations are already propagated to AWS, the editing is either a single-step process (if the changes were never propagated to AWS) or a two-step process (if the changes were propagated at least once).

- Step 1: In the Deception Admin Portal
- Step 2: In the AWS Cloud

## Deleting an AWS Account

Depending on whether the configurations are already propagated to AWS, the deletion is either a single-step process (if the changes were never propagated to AWS) or a two-step process (if the changes were propagated at least once).

You can delete AWS deception settings only if no AWS decoys are deployed. If you have already deployed AWS decoys, you must delete all decoys and complete the deletion in AWS cloud first (via Terraform or CloudShell script) before deleting the settings.

- Step 1: In the Deception Admin Portal
- Step 2: In the AWS Cloud

To initiate editing in the Deception Admin Portal:​​​​​

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **AWS**> **Settings**.
2. Locate the account that you want to edit, and click the **Edit**icon. See image. The **AWS Account Setting**window appears.
3. In the **AWS Account Setting**window: See image.
  - **Enabled**: Select to modify the status of Cloud Deception for the AWS account.
  - **Enable GenAI Prompt Logging**: Select to modify the status of logging prompts and responses from [generative AI (Gen AI) decoys in AWS](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/creating-generative-ai-decoy-aws). The prompts and responses are recorded in the aws `gen ai input` and `aws gen ai ouput` on the [ThreatParse page](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/viewing-threatparse-details) with the **AWS GenAI Model was Invoked** rule. When logging is enabled, an S3 bucket is created to store prompts and responses from the Gen AI models. This S3 bucket collects prompts and responses from all Gen AI applications in that AWS account, including the legitimate Gen AI applications. However, only those prompts and responses pertaining to the Gen AI decoys created by Deception are sent to the Deception Admin Portal. If you want to avoid storing (temporary) prompts and responses from the legitimate Gen AI applications in the S3 bucket, ensure that the Gen AI decoys are deployed in a different AWS account that does not contain any legitimate Gen AI applications.
  - **Tags**: Click to configure tags for AWS resources. To learn more, see [Creating and Managing Tags for AWS Resources](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/creating-and-managing-tags-aws).
4. Click **Save**.

To complete editing in AWS Cloud, choose a method based on how the integration was configured:

- Terraform-based deployment
- CloudShell-based deployment

1. On the **Cloud Deception - AWS** page, go to **Settings**.
2. Locate the AWS account you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
4. Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the `aws-decoys.tf.json` file in a text editor.
5. Locate the `backend` block in the `aws-decoys.tf.json` file. Add your back-end details and save the file. The following example shows a `backend` block of an S3 bucket-based Terraform back end: `{ "terraform": { "backend": { "s3": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate", "region": "us-east-1", "encrypt": true } } } }`Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same AWS account.
6. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
7. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
8. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted.
9. The necessary resources are deployed, and a JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
10. On the **Cloud Deception - AWS** page, go to **Settings**, locate the AWS account you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
11. Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
2. Launch AWS CloudShell. See image. The **CloudShell**window appears.
3. In the **CloudShell** window: See image.
  1. Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the [automated download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-aws#zd-direct-download-script-aws) or [manual download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-aws#zd-manual-download-script-aws).
  2. When prompted to continue with deletion, enter `y` and press `Enter.` If you enter `n`and press `Enter`, then the deletion process is aborted, and the configuration is enabled again in the Deception Admin Portal.

To initiate deletion in the Deception Admin Portal:​​​​​

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **AWS**> **Settings**.
2. Locate the account that you want to delete, and click the **Delete**icon.

See image.

All decoys are marked for deletion and the configuration is disabled in the Deception Admin Portal.

If you have never run the deployment script on AWS or used the Terraform commands, then the deletion process is completed with this step. If you have already used either of them to sync the settings or deploy decoys, then proceed to [Step 2](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/deleting-aws-deception-settings#zd-aws-portal-delete) to complete the deletion process.

To complete deletion in the AWS Cloud, choose a method based on how the integration was configured:

- Terraform-based deployment
- CloudShell-based deployment

On the **Cloud Deception - AWS** page, go to **Settings**.

1. Locate the AWS account you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
2. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
3. Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the `aws-decoys.tf.json` file in a text editor.
4. Locate the `backend` block in the `aws-decoys.tf.json` file. Add your back-end details and save the file. The following example shows a `backend` block of an S3 bucket-based Terraform back end: `{ "terraform": { "backend": { "s3": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate", "region": "us-east-1", "encrypt": true } } } }`Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same AWS account.
5. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
6. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
7. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted.
8. The necessary resources are deployed, and a JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
9. On the **Cloud Deception - AWS** page, go to **Settings**, locate the AWS account you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
10. Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
2. Launch AWS CloudShell. See image. The **CloudShell**window appears.
3. In the **CloudShell** window: See image.
  1. Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the [automated download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-aws#zd-direct-download-script-aws) or [manual download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-aws#zd-manual-download-script-aws).
  2. When prompted to continue with deletion, enter `y` and press `Enter.` If you enter `n`and press `Enter`, then the deletion process is aborted, and the configuration is enabled again in the Deception Admin Portal.

In some cases, the deployment script might fail to remove the entries of the AWS resources that were marked for deletion in the Deception Admin Portal. For example, manually removing AWS resources deployed by Deception from the AWS cloud can fail to remove entries of resources from the Deception Admin Portal if the resources are interdependent. If the deployment script fails to remove these entries, you need to use the **Force Delete**option.

- See instructions.

1. In the Deception Admin Portal, go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **AWS**> **Settings**.
2. Click **Force Delete**. This option appears when the deletion process is started. See image.
3. Confirm your action. The AWS resource entries are removed from the Deception Admin Portal.

## Editing an Azure Account

You can edit a Microsoft Azure account from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. Depending on whether the configurations are already propagated to Azure, the editing is either a single-step process (if the deployment script was never used on Azure) or a two-step process (if the deployment script was used at least once).

- Step 1: In the Deception Admin Portal
- Step 2: In the Microsoft Azure Portal

## Deleting an Azure Account

You can delete Cloud Deception settings configured for a Microsoft Azure account from the Deception Admin Portal. Depending on if the configurations are already propagated to Azure, the deletion is either a single-step process (if the deployment script was never used on Azure) or a two-step process (if the deployment script was used at least once).

You can delete Azure Cloud Deception settings only if no Azure decoys are deployed. If you have already deployed Azure decoys, you must delete all decoys and run the deployment script first before deleting the settings.

- Step 2: In the Microsoft Azure Portal

2. Locate the account that you want to edit, and click the **Edit**icon. See image. The **Azure Account Setting** window appears.
3. In the **Azure Account Setting**window: See image.
  - **Enabled**: Select to modify the status of Cloud Deception for the Azure account.
  - **Region**: Select a new region for the Azure account from the drop-down menu.
  - **Decoy Manager Resource Group**: Enter a new name or update the existing one.
4. Click **Save**.

To complete editing in Azure cloud, choose a method based on how the integration was configured:

- Terraform-based deployment
- Cloud Shell-based deployment

1. On the **Cloud Deception - Azure**page, go to **Settings**.
2. Locate the Azure account you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.

6. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
7. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
8. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted. The necessary resources are deployed.
9. Run the following command to download the details of the state as a JSON file. `terraform output -json decoys_output > deployment-output.json`A JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
10. On the **Cloud Deception - Azure**page, go to **Settings**, locate the Azure account you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
11. Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.

1. Sign in to the [Azure Portal](http://https//portal.azure.com).
2. Launch Cloud Shell by clicking the **Cloud Shell** icon on the top navigation bar. See image. The **Cloud Shell** window appears.
3. In the **Cloud Shell** window:
  1. Set your shell environment to PowerShell.
  2. Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the [automated download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-direct-download-script) or [manual download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-manual-download-script).
  3. Enter the option to sync settings.

To initiate deletion in the Deception Admin Portal:​​​​​

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **Azure**> **Settings**.
2. Locate the Azure account that must be deleted, and click the **Delete**icon. See image.

All fields are deleted, and the configuration is disabled in the Deception Admin Portal.

If you have never run the deployment script on Azure, then the deletion process is completed with this step. If you have already used the deployment script either to sync the settings or deploy decoys, then proceed to Step 2 to complete the deletion process.

To complete deletion in the Azure Cloud, choose a method based on how the integration was configured:

- Terraform-based deployment
- Cloud Shell-based deployment

1. On the **Cloud Deception - Azure**page, go to **Settings**.
2. Locate the Azure account you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
4. Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the `azure-decoys.tf.json` file in a text editor.
5. Locate the `backend` block in the `azure-decoys.tf.json` file. Add your back-end details and save the file. The following example shows a `backend` block of an Azure blob storage-based Terraform back end: `{ "terraform": { "backend": { "azurerm": { "resource_group_name": "your-tfstate-rg", "storage_account_name": "yourtfstatestorageacct", "container_name": "tfstate", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate" } } } }`Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same Azure account.
6. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
7. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
8. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted. The necessary resources are deployed.
9. Run the following command to download the details of the state as a JSON file. `terraform output -json decoys_output > deployment-output.json`A JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
10. On the **Cloud Deception - Azure**page, go to **Settings**, locate the Azure account you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
11. Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.

1. Sign in to the [Azure Portal](http://https//portal.azure.com).
2. Launch Cloud Shell by clicking the **Cloud Shell** icon on the top navigation bar. See image. The **Cloud Shell** window appears.
3. In the **Cloud Shell** window: See image.
  1. Set your shell environment to PowerShell.
  2. Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the [automated download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-direct-download-script) or [manual download method](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/obtaining-deployment-script-azure#zd-manual-download-script).
  3. When prompted to continue with deletion, enter `y` and press `Enter.` If you enter `n` and press `Enter`, then the deletion process is aborted, and the configuration is enabled again in the Deception Admin Portal.

All resources created for [setting up Cloud Deception with Azure](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/setting-cloud-deception-microsoft-azure) are deleted.

In some cases, the deployment script might fail to remove the entries of the Azure resources that were marked for deletion in the Deception Admin Portal. For example, manually removing Azure resources deployed by Deception from the Azure cloud can fail to remove entries of resources from the Deception Admin Portal if the resources are interdependent. If the deployment script fails to remove these entries, you need to use the **Force Delete**option.

- Steps to Force Delete Azure Settings

1. In the Deception Admin Portal, go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **Azure**> **Settings**.
2. Click **Force Delete**. This option appears when the deletion process is started. See image.
3. Confirm your action. The Azure resource entries are removed from the Deception Admin Portal.

## Managing Cloud Deception Settings for a GCP Project

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/managing-cloud-deception-settings-gcp-project
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Deceive  > Cloud Deception > GCP > Managing Cloud Deception Settings for a GCP Project
- Last modified: 2026-07-04T07:06Z
- Summary: How to edit or delete a GCP Cloud Deception project.

You can edit or delete Cloud Deception settings configured for your Google Cloud Deception (GCP) projects from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

## Editing a GCP Project

Depending on whether the configurations are already propagated to GCP, editing a GCP project is either a single-step process (if the changes were never propagated to GCP) or a two-step process (if the changes were propagated at least once).

- Step 1: In the Deception Admin Portal
- Step 2: In the GCP Cloud

## Deleting a GCP Project

Depending on whether the configurations are already propagated to GCP, deleting a GCP project is either a single-step process (if the changes were never propagated to GCP) or a two-step process (if the changes were propagated at least once).

You can delete GCP deception settings only if no GCP decoys are deployed. If you have already deployed GCP decoys, you must delete all decoys and complete the deletion in the GCP cloud first before deleting the settings.

- Step 1: In the Deception Admin Portal
- Step 2: In the GCP Cloud

To initiate editing in the Deception Admin Portal:​​​​​

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **GCP**> **Settings**.
2. Locate the project that you want to edit, and click the **Edit**icon. See image. The **GCP Project Setting**drawer appears.
3. In the **GCP Project Setting**drawer, select **Enabled**to modify the status of Cloud Deception for the GCP project. See image.
4. Click **Save**.

To complete editing in the GCP cloud:

1. On the **Cloud Deception - GCP**page, go to **Settings**.
2. Locate the GCP project you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
4. Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the `gcp-decoys.tf.json` file in a text editor.
5. Locate the `backend` block in the `gxp-decoys.tf.json` file. Add your back-end details and save the file. The following example shows a `backend` block of Google Cloud Storage bucket-based Terraform back end: `{ "terraform": { "backend": { "gcs": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "prefix": "deception/terraform" } } } }`Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same GCP project.
6. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and set the user agent for Terraform: `export TF_APPEND_USER_AGENT="<value_from_ui>"`
7. Run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
8. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
9. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted. The necessary resources are deployed.
10. Run the following command to export the state file as JSON: `terraform output -json gcp_terraform_output > deployment-output.json`The JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
11. On the **Cloud Deception - GCP**page, go to **Settings**, locate the GCP project you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
12. Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.

To initiate deletion in the Deception Admin Portal:​​​​​

1. Go to **Deceive**> **Cloud Deception**> **GCP**> **Settings**.
2. Locate the project that you want to delete, and click the **Delete**icon.

See image.

All decoys are marked for deletion, and the configuration is disabled in the Deception Admin Portal.

If you have never run the Terraform commands, then the deletion process is completed with this step. If you have already used either of them to sync the settings or deploy decoys, then proceed to the next step to complete the deletion process.

To complete deletion in the GCP cloud:

1. On the **Cloud Deception - GCP**page, go to **Settings**.
2. Locate the GCP project you added, and click the **Download**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
3. In the **Terraform Deployment Steps**window, click **Download**to download the necessary files. See image. A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
4. Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the `gcp-decoys.tf.json` file in a text editor.
5. Locate the `backend` block in the `gcp-decoys.tf.json` file. Add your back-end details and save the file. The following example shows a `backend` block of Google Cloud Storage bucket-based Terraform back end: `{ "terraform": { "backend": { "gcs": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "prefix": "deception/terraform" } } } }`Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same GCP project.
6. In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and set the user agent for Terraform: `export TF_APPEND_USER_AGENT="<value_from_ui>"`
7. Run the following command to create a new workspace: ``terraform init && terraform workspace new``<workspace_name>``
8. Run the following command to deploy resources: `terraform apply`
9. Review the plan, and confirm it by entering `Yes` when prompted. The necessary resources are selected.
10. Run the following command to export the state file as JSON: `terraform output -json gcp_terraform_output > deployment-output.json`The JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
11. On the **Cloud Deception - GCP**page, go to **Settings**, locate the GCP project you added, and click the **Upload**icon in the **Actions**column. See image.
12. Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.

## Managing Decoy Connectors

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/deception/managing-decoy-connectors
- Product: Deception
- Path: Deception Help > Settings > Topology > Decoy Connectors > Managing Decoy Connectors
- Last modified: 2026-08-03T00:19Z
- Summary: How to manage Decoy Connectors in the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

You can perform the following actions on a Decoy Connector:

- Obtain Decoy Connector Recovery and Diagnostics Credentials
- Reboot a Decoy Connector
- View Decoy Connector Update Logs
- Download Decoy Connector Debug Logs
- Edit or Delete a Decoy Connector

After you [add and connect a Decoy Connector to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/adding-connecting-decoy-connector-admin-portal), its recovery and diagnostic passwords are randomized. You can obtain the new credentials from the Deception Admin Portal.

Only users with the super admin role can view recovery credentials. To learn more, see [About Users & Roles](https://help.zscaler.com/deception/about-users-roles#deception-user-role-about-role).

To obtain the recovery and diagnostics credentials:

1. Go to **Settings** > **Topology** > **Decoy Connectors.**
2. Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click **Actions** > **Credentials**. See image.
3. Copy the required credentials, and click **Close**. See image.

You can reboot a configured Decoy Connector in the Deception Admin Portal.

To reboot a Decoy Connector:

1. Go to **Settings** > **Topology** > **Decoy Connectors.**
2. Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click **Actions** > **Reboot**. See image.
3. In the confirmation window, click **OK**.

You can use the update logs to troubleshoot issues related to Decoy Connector updates.

To view the update logs:

1. Go to **Settings** > **Topology** > **Decoy Connectors**.
2. Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click **Logs > View update logs.** See image.
3. View the logs as necessary, and then click **Close**. See image.

Debug logs are system-generated logs that are stored on a Decoy Connector. Debug logs are copied to the Deception Admin Portal when you initiate a download request. The logs contain timestamps and messages that help you troubleshoot any issues with network decoys or other integrations that use Decoy Connectors.

For a Decoy Connector, you can download either the most recent or all debug logs.

Make sure that the Decoy Connector is connected to the Deception Admin Portal before you download the debug logs.

To download debug logs:

1. Go to **Settings** > **Topology** > **Decoy Connectors**.
2. Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click **Logs**.
3. Select an option from the **Logs** drop-down menu: See image.
  - **Request recent debug logs**: Download the last 1,000 lines from each log file.
  - **Request all debug logs**: Download the complete log files.
4. After the request is initiated and completed, click **Download debug logs**.
5. In the **Debug Logs** window, click the **Download** icon. See image. The debug logs are downloaded as a .tar.xz file. Extract the file using a file compression tool (e.g., WinZip, 7-zip, etc.). If the debug log files consume a large amount of disk space, you can periodically delete them. Click the **Delete** icon to delete the logs from the Deception Admin Portal. See image.
6. Click **Close**.

You can edit or delete a configured Decoy Connector in the Deception Admin Portal.

Deception uses Private Access (ZPA) or Threat Intelligence Decoy Connectors to deploy decoys in a dedicated Deception cloud. You cannot edit or delete them. Contact Zscaler Support to manage them.

## Edit a Decoy Connector

To edit a Decoy Connector:

1. Go to **Settings** > **Topology** > **Decoy Connectors**.
2. Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click **Actions** > **Edit**. See image.
3. In the **Decoy Connector Details** window, modify the required values. See image.
4. Click **Save**.

## Delete a Decoy Connector

To delete a Decoy Connector:

1. Go to **Settings** > **Topology** > **Decoy Connectors**.
2. Locate the required Decoy Connector, and then click **Actions** > **Delete**. See image.
3. In the confirmation window, click **OK**.
